svg.title: Control plane identities and their writes
svg.desc: Identities of ADR-0038, proposed and not built. In each spoke, the analyzer, executor and verifier keep the writes that invariant 6 gives them today. The new spoke identity shadewright-reporter reads Incidents and RemediationRequests in the operator namespace, plus get on remediationsettings and get on the kube-system Namespace by resource name. It writes nothing in the cluster, and has no Secrets, no Git identity and no model credential. Its egress is DNS, the API server and TCP 443 for the hub, whose host is pinned in its settings, because a NetworkPolicy cannot match host names. It sends one snapshot at a time over HTTPS to the hub intake service, the only line from spoke to hub. At the hub, intake reads Cluster objects and the hub settings, and creates or updates only the one snapshot object of the verified cluster in the hub namespace, in one write with a version check. It allows one request in flight per cluster, a report rate and a size cap, refuses a snapshot the redactor would change or cannot finish within its budget, and pauses when the hub settings are missing or invalid. RBAC does not separate spokes: that guard is intake code, and it needs tests. Intake terminates TLS itself, has no write on Cluster objects, no Git write, no model credential and makes no external call. The fleet controller alone writes Cluster status, including the issuer keys it fetches for discovery clusters over DNS and port 443 behind the dial guard; it reads the snapshots and deletes a snapshot of an earlier registration. It creates no Namespace or RoleBinding and holds no bind or escalate. The status page has its own identity in its own namespace with a default-deny NetworkPolicy, listens on 127.0.0.1 only, is reached by port-forward and only reads Cluster objects and snapshots. A person runs the registration command, which reads the spoke identity live, and people who may merge in the hub GitOps repository approve each new spoke, which adds only its Cluster object, and revoke it by setting revoked to true. No hub identity is cluster-admin, and none has a model credential or a Git write identity in phase 1.

One hub namespace holds one snapshot per spoke; RBAC does not separate spokes, intake's code does. No hub identity is cluster-admin.
No hub component has a model credential or a Git write identity in phase 1. Limiting hub egress to the API server needs an operator ipBlock or CNI rule.
Each spoke has its own model credential (key: ADR-0037) and daily budget (ADR-0023).
